Position Summary:

The Director of Pharmacy Operations & Accreditation is a senior leadership role responsible for the strategic design, development, and operational execution of retail, specialty, and ambulatory pharmacy programs across health-system partner sites nationwide. This role oversees critical pillars of the business—pharmacy design/build and national accreditation—while serving as a trusted operational and strategic partner to both internal teams and external health-system executives.

The Director will lead complex pharmacy build initiatives from concept through operational readiness, ensure accreditation excellence across all programs, and navigate sophisticated client dynamics with diplomacy, technical expertise, and a solutions-oriented mindset. Success in this role requires a balance of strategic vision, operational rigor, and exceptional stakeholder management. The Director serves as a senior escalation point for complex, high-stakes client challenges, bringing advanced communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills to de-escalate issues and align diverse stakeholders. This role proactively anticipates operational and client risks, addressing concerns early to protect partnerships and ensure successful outcomes.

Pharmacy Design & Construction:

  • Provide executive-level, end-to-end oversight of the design, development, and build-out of retail, specialty, and ambulatory pharmacy programs at health-system partner sites.

  • Lead and manage the on-site pharmacy builds and launch teams who serve as the first operational presence within new health-system partnerships.

  • Cultivate strong, trusted relationships between on-site teams and health-system stakeholders, ensuring Clearway is positioned as a credible, collaborative, and value-driven partner from day one.

  • Ensure pharmacy designs and build strategies align with regulatory requirements, accreditation standards, clinical workflows, and long-term operational sustainability.

  • Guide teams through go-live, early operations, and stabilization, ensuring a seamless transition from building phase to ongoing operational ownership.

  • Work in close partnership with the Client Services team to support the transition of newly built or launched pharmacies into stable, high-performing operations.

  • Provide operational leadership during handoff phases, ensuring clarity of ownership, accountability, and performance expectations.

  • Support client-facing teams in managing ongoing relationships with health-system partners, reinforcing trust, credibility, and operational excellence.

  • Act as an executive presence with health-system leaders during critical transition, optimization, or remediation phases.

  • Foster a culture of operational excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Accreditation Leadership:

  • Lead, oversee, and develop the accreditation team, creating strategic vision and ensuring consistent, high-quality execution across all pharmacy programs.

  • Own the enterprise-wide accreditation strategy, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and evolving regulatory and quality standards.

  • Ensure that all pharmacies and programs are fully prepared for initial accreditation, re-accreditation, audits, and site visits (e.g., URAC, ACHC).

  • Embed accreditation requirements into pharmacy design, operational workflows, and quality management systems.

  • Drive accountability, readiness, and continuous improvement across the accreditation function.

Strategic & Operational Leadership:

  • Serve as the subject matter expert for retail, specialty, and ambulatory pharmacy operations, programs, and services.

  • Lead strategic planning efforts to evolve pharmacy services in alignment with health-system needs, patient outcomes, and Clearway’s growth objectives.

  • Conduct on-site operational assessments to identify performance gaps, optimization opportunities, and improvement initiatives.

  • Partner cross-functionally to identify future expansion opportunities and develop site-specific operational strategies.

  • Partner closely with the Director of Client Analytics to define, develop, and operationalize reporting frameworks that demonstrate pharmacy performance, value creation, and financial impact.

  • Translate operational performance data into clear, actionable insights for internal leadership and external health-system stakeholders.

  • Oversee the development and refinement of dashboards, KPIs, and performance metrics that support business cases, accreditation readiness, and continuous improvement.

  • Ensure operational data supports strategic decision-making, client storytelling, and long-term program sustainability.

Education:

  • Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree required.

  • A master’s degree in healthcare management or business administration is highly preferred

Experience:

  • 7+ years of relevant experience in retail, specialty and ambulatory pharmacy are required.

  • At least 5+ years in a supervisory/leadership capacity

  • Proficiency in EMR/EHR systems is preferred

Certificates / Licenses:

  • Active and unrestricted license to practice pharmacy in at least 1 state

  • Ability to be multi-state licensed preferred

  • Active preceptor license or ability to obtain within 12 months of hire

  • CSP Highly desired

Knowledge/Skills:

  • Deep expertise in retail, specialty, and ambulatory pharmacy operations, including pharmacy procedures, dispensing systems, EHR/EMR platforms, and supporting technologies.

  • Proven leadership experience overseeing complex pharmacy operations, programs, and cross-functional initiatives, with the ability to drive execution at scale.

  • Strong analytical and financial acumen, including the ability to assess performance, identify optimization opportunities, and develop metrics, business cases, and value/savings models.

  • Demonstrated excellence in people leadership, organizational design, and performance management to drive accountability, efficiency, and continuous improvement.

  • Exceptional communication, negotiation, and conflict-management skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across internal teams and external stakeholders.

  • Highly self-directed and solutions-oriented leader with strong prioritization, judgment, and problem-solving capabilities, particularly in fast-paced or resource-constrained environments.

Special Working Conditions (On-call, travel, shift, coverage):

  • This role may require up to 20% travel

  • Clearway Health Specialty Pharmacies, serving patients in hospitals, health systems, and communities, may require employees at client sites to work on company-recognized holidays, with eligibility for holiday pay.   

This information is being provided to promote pay transparency and equal employment opportunities at Clearway Health. The current annual compensation range for this position is $153,000 - $190,000. The actual rate within this range that you will be offered will depend on a variety of factors including geography, skills and abilities, education, experience and other relevant factors.

We are seeking an Insight Associate Director to join our global analytics and insights practice based in London or Edinburgh. This is a mid-senior role responsible for owning and scaling large‑scale social intelligence, audience analytics, and primary research insight engagements across a portfolio of Real Chemistry’s priority UK and EMEA Medical Education clients.

jobs.title: Lead Clinical Pharmacist
jobs.description_html:
Based in San Francisco, Arine is a rapidly growing healthcare technology and clinical services company with a mission to ensure individuals receive the safest and most effective treatments for their unique and evolving healthcare needs. 

Frequently, medications cause more harm than good. Incorrect drugs and doses costs the US healthcare system over $528 billion in waste, avoidable harm, and hospitalizations each year. Arine is redefining what excellent healthcare looks like by solving these issues through our software platform (SaaS). We combine cutting edge data science, machine learning, AI, and deep clinical expertise to introduce a patient-centric view to medication management, and develop and deliver personalized care plans on a massive scale for patients and their care teams.

Arine is committed to improving the lives and health of complex patients that have an outsized impact on healthcare costs and have traditionally been difficult to identify and address. These patients face numerous challenges including complicated prescribing issues across multiple medications and providers, medication challenges with many chronic diseases, and patient issues with access to care. Backed by leading healthcare investors and collaborating with top healthcare organizations and providers, we deliver recommendations and facilitate clinical interventions that lead to significant, measurable health improvements for patients and cost savings for customers. 

Why is Arine a Great Place to Work?:

Outstanding Team and Culture - Our shared mission unites and motivates us to do our best work. We have a relentless passion and commitment to the innovation required to be the market leader in medication intelligence.

Making a Proven Difference in Healthcare - We are saving patient lives, and enabling individuals to experience improved health outcomes, including significant reductions in hospitalizations and cost of care.

Market Opportunity - Arine is backed by leading healthcare investors and was founded to tackle one of the largest healthcare problems today. Non-optimized medications therapies which cost the US 275,000 lives and $528 billion annually.

Dramatic Growth - Arine is managing more than 18 million lives across prominent health plans after only 4 years in the market, and was ranked 236 on the 2024 Inc. 5000 list and was named the 5th fastest-growing company in the AI category.

The Role:

We are looking for a Lead Clinical Pharmacist to assist in leading one of the clinical teams that uses the Arine platform to deliver excellent outcomes for our customers. 

The Lead Clinical Pharmacist is part of a team of clinicians, analysts, clinical support staff, and trainees utilizing Arine’s software platform to help optimize patient outcomes for our clients. The purpose of the Lead Clinical Pharmacist position is to assist in managing a patient engagement program that achieves four and five-star results across a variety of Medicare Part C and Part D measures. The position leads and oversees expert level medication therapy consultation to patients and providers, collaborates with the Engineering team and leadership to improve Arine’s software platform, and supervises a team of Pharmacists who are directly reviewing medication profiles and counseling patients, interacting with other health professionals to help improve patient outcomes. The Lead Clinical Pharmacist partners with the Clinical Support Lead to achieve results by setting a strategic approach with Arine leadership and with other Clinical Care Leads to drive excellent medication outcomes and by engaging client teams and Arine Customer Success to align expectations and communicate roadblocks and progress. 

This role encompasses all of Arine's Clinical Care team activities. Lead Clinical Pharmacists will be asked to:

  • Support oversight of goals, progress, and resource allocation of an Arine full-service clinical project
  • Develop intervention strategies to optimize medication regimens to improve health outcomes (example, decrease hospitalizations, cost, and morbidity),  support CMS quality measures (example adherence, SUPD and SPC), and other established goals
  • Manage team productivity and timelines to ensure goals are met 
  • Ensure quality assurance standards are met
  • Develop new workflows, best practices, and standards to drive continuous improvement in health outcomes, efficiencies, and insights to improve our product 
  • Prioritize project needs and be able to communicate the magnitude of potential impacts when escalating product asks, staffing requests, etc
  • Represent Arine’s Clinical Care team at customer meetings, as well as lead internal staff meetings
  • Hire, train, and schedule team members and help lead in the growth and development of the team
  • Manage and conduct performance reviews for assigned team members
  • Respond to questions by patients, providers, and other professional personnel and team members
  • Comply with all company policies and state and federal rules and regulations

Who You Are and What You Bring:

  • At least 12 months experience in a Pharmacist role on Adherence or MTM projects, with a track record of excellence and demonstrated leadership (required)
  • Team management and or coaching experience 
  • Excellent analytical skills
  • Ability to quickly problem solve and triage both clinical and operational situations 
  • Ability to organize and set priorities which accurately reflect the relative importance of job responsibilities
  • Excellent communication and project management skills
  • Ability to engage with the patients, promote adherence and treat patients with empathy and compassion
  • Strong grasp of standard workflows for medication adherence 
  • Ability to apply judgment and make informed decisions in order to work independently and meet deadlines
  • Ability to work effectively within a team and foster effective working relationships and build consensus
  • Eagerness to learn new skills in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
  • Strong computer skills, including facility with Microsoft Word, Excel, Google Spreadsheets, and Google Documents

Remote Work Requirements:

  • An established private work area that ensures information privacy

  • A stable high-speed internet connection for telephonic and/or remote work

  • This role is remote, but you will be required to come to on-site meetings multiple times per year. This may be in the interview process, onboarding, and team meetings

Perks:

Joining Arine offers you a dynamic role and the opportunity to contribute to the company's growth and shape its future. You'll have unparalleled learning and growth prospects, collaborating closely with experienced Clinicians, Engineers, Software Architects, and Digital Health Entrepreneurs.

The posted range represents the annual base salary range for this position and does not include any other potential components of the compensation package, benefits, and perks. Ultimately, the final pay decision will consider factors such as your experience, job level, location, and other relevant job-related criteria. The annual base salary range for this position is $140,000 - $147,000.

Job Requirements:

  • Ability to pass a background check
  • Must live in and be eligible to work in the United States

Information Security Roles and Responsibilities:

All staff at Arine are expected to be part of its Information Security Management Program and undergo periodic training on Information Security Awareness and HIPAA guidelines. Each user is responsible to maintain a secure working environment and follow all policies and procedures. Upon hire, each person is assigned and must complete trainings before access is granted for their specific role within Arine.

Arine is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where all employees are treated with fairness and respect. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, or any other legally protected status. Our hiring decisions and employment practices are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply and join us in our mission.

jobs.title: Pharmacy Network Support Associate
jobs.description_html:
Who We Are:

SmithRx is a rapidly growing, venture-backed Health-Tech company.  Our mission is to disrupt the expensive and inefficient Pharmacy Benefit Management (PBM) sector by building a next-generation drug acquisition platform driven by cutting edge technology, innovative cost saving tools, and best-in-class customer service.  With hundreds of thousands of members onboarded since 2016, SmithRx has a solution that is resonating with clients all across the country.

We pride ourselves for our mission-driven and collaborative culture that inspires our employees to do their best work. We believe that the U.S healthcare system is in need of transformation, and we come to work each day dedicated to making that change a reality. At our core, we are guided by our company values:

  • Integrity: Our purpose guides our actions and gives us confidence in the path ahead. With unwavering honesty and dependability, we embrace the pressure of challenging the old and exemplify ethical leadership to create the new.
  • Courage: We face continuous challenges with grit and resilience. We embrace the discomfort of the unknown by balancing autonomy with empathy, and ownership with vulnerability. We boldly challenge the status quo to keep moving forward—always.
  • Together: The success of SmithRx reflects the strength of our partnerships and the commitment of our team. Our shared values bind us together and make us one. When one falls, we all fall; when one rises, we all rise.

Job Summary:

The Pharmacy Network Team serves as the strategic link between our members and high-quality care. We manage the end-to-end lifecycle of our pharmacy partnerships - balancing competitive pricing and network strategy with rigorous credentialing and regulatory compliance. By fostering collaborative provider relations, we minimize operational complexity and optimize health outcomes, serving as a critical pillar in the SmithRx mission to navigate the evolving healthcare landscape. 

The Pharmacy Network Support Associate role involves supporting the Pharmacy Network Team in day-to-day tasks, managing relationships between pharmacies and network providers, onboarding new pharmacies, and providing support to existing pharmacies. The position requires close collaboration with valued pharmacy partners and internal cross-functional teams within the SmithRx organization. This role serves as a key point of contact for resolving internal and external escalations efficiently to maintain seamless service across the network.

What you will do:

  • Building and maintaining strong relationships with pharmacy providers, addressing escalations, and facilitating effective communication between the pharmacy and the organization. 
  • Manage and resolve pharmacy escalations by gathering the necessary information, collaborating with internal teams, and coordinating subsequent follow-up communications. 
  • Resolving any issues or conflicts that arise between the organization and pharmacy providers. This may involve investigating complaints, conducting root cause analysis, and working collaboratively with internal teams and providers to find effective solutions. 
  • Helps orchestrate incoming communications within the Pharmacy Network Distribution inbox, ensuring inquiries are accurately triaged, tracked, and resolved within a timely fashion.
  • Act as the administrative owner of the Pharmacy Network Jira board, routing tasks to the appropriate teams to ensure swift resolution of network issues according to established SLAs. 
  • Assists in managing the end-to-end network satisfaction survey, preparing materials and targeted questions, distributing to external partners, monitoring response rates and translating feedback into actionable improvement plans.
  • Escalate pharmacy concerns internally and to help solve complex issues. 
  • Assist with building out a Knowledge Base and contribute to our ongoing process improvement efforts.

What you will bring to SmithRx:

  • High school diploma or equivalent is required. Some college coursework or a relevant certification is a plus.
  • 1-2 years of focused administrative support experience in a healthcare, compliance, or credentialing environment is highly preferred.
  • Exceptional organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail, with a proven ability to manage multiple priorities and meet tight deadlines in a fast-paced setting.
  • Strong proficiency in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office Suite (especially MS Excel/Google Sheets) and the ability to rapidly learn new enterprise software (e.g., Jira).
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills essential for clear correspondence with network providers and internal stakeholders.
  • A self-driven, motivated, and highly proactive individual who takes initiative to anticipate needs and problem-solve independently.
  • Proven capacity to identify and resolve complex administrative issues, escalate concerns appropriately, and recommend effective process improvements.

What SmithRx Offers You: 

  • Highly competitive wellness benefits including Medical, Pharmacy, Dental and Vision Insurance. SmithRx pays up to 90% for you and your family.
  • Fully paid Life insurance and Disability benefits
  • 3 weeks PTO
  • 401(k) Retirement Savings Program
  • Flexible Spending Benefits
  • Generous Paid Parental Leave benefits
  • Professional development, training and career growth opportunities
  • Well-stocked kitchen in office locations

jobs.title: Pharmacist (Remote)
jobs.description_html:
Founded in San Francisco in 2011, The Apothecarium began as a patient-focused medical dispensary and has grown into a trusted, award-winning cannabis retail brand with locations across California, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and New Jersey.

We’re known for our modern, welcoming spaces, emphasis on education, and unmatched customer service. Whether you're new to cannabis or a seasoned consumer, our highly trained cannabis associates are here to provide personalized, one-on-one consultations to help you find the products that best meet your needs.

We don’t just sell cannabis — we create experiences that promote wellness, build trust, and enrich lives. Come see why so many patients and customers choose The Apothecarium as their go-to destination for cannabis.

The Cannabis Dispensary Pharmacist is a key member of our dispensary team, responsible for ensuring the safe and compliant dispensing of medical cannabis to patients in accordance with Pennsylvania’s Medical Marijuana Program. This position involves providing expert guidance on cannabis therapies, verifying physician certifications, and ensuring accurate patient records. The pharmacist will lead patient consultations, educating them on the therapeutic use of medical cannabis, and recommend appropriate forms of consumption based on individual medical needs. The role also includes maintaining compliance with state regulations and collaborating with dispensary staff to optimize patient care and dispensary operations.

Responsibilities:

  • Conduct one-on-one patient consultations to provide education on medical cannabis, discuss consumption methods, and recommend appropriate treatments based on physician certifications.
  • Maintain accurate and confidential patient records, documenting consultations, recommendations, and any relevant information while adhering to privacy and data protection regulations.
  • Ensure strict compliance with Pennsylvania Medical Marijuana laws and dispensary regulations, including maintaining accurate records, verifying patient certifications, and managing the Prescription Monitoring Program.
  • Dispense medical cannabis products according to physician recommendations and patient needs, ensuring proper use and dosage.
  • Stay updated on the latest research in cannabis pharmacology, contributing to patient care with evidence-based recommendations and industry developments.
  • Collaborate with the Dispensary General Managers and other team members to ensure smooth operations and achieve key performance metrics.

Experience & Requirements:

  • Valid Pennsylvania Pharmacist license, in good standing.
  • Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy or PharmD.
  • 1+ years experience working in a pharmacy setting assisting patients/customers.
  • Satisfactory completion of any State-required Medical Cannabis education programs.

jobs.title: Clinical Pharmacist, Pharmacy
jobs.description_html:
Built on meritocracy, our unique company culture rewards self-starters and those who are committed to doing what is best for our customers.

As a Clinical Pharmacist, you will collaborate with Client Engagement team (client support team) and Brown & Brown Clients to provide clinical expertise and clinical analytics support. You will interpret and evaluate pharmacy claims trends, provide clinical insights, and recommend clinical management strategies and solutions. You will bring strong industry knowledge and will serve as a trusted business partner to your clients. A successful candidate is a team player who is creative, organized, detailed oriented, pro-active and have strong communication skills.

Essential Duties and Functions:

  • Derive data-driven strategy recommendations regarding formulary coverage, utilization management, plan design, clinical programs, etc. that align with client goals and culture
  • Review, analyze and present clinical analysis to support internal & external business goals
  • Support in developing and communicating clinical insight to key stakeholders including clients, brokers, and internal teammates
  • Collaborate across teams and within the broader Brown & Brown organization to support growth, new business, and client retention
  • Maintain current knowledge of pharmacy/medical trends within the healthcare setting
  • Follow and assess clinical updates in the healthcare setting including but not limited to FDA-related changes, key PBM (pharmacy benefit manager) partners, state and federal legislative bodies, Wolters Kluwer/Medi-Span and key healthcare communication sources
  • Assist in the development of new clinical pharmacy services product offerings and clinical marketing collateral to be distributed to clients and other marketing channels (i.e. website, blog, videos, white papers, etc.)
  • Support in providing expertise in the specific formulary requirements established for commercial, Medicare, Exchange and Medicaid programs
  • Support clients with any quality measure initiatives (i.e. Medicare Star Ratings or HEDIS measures), as requested
  • Comprehend and evaluate clinical program value proposition to clients
  • Mentor and support non-clinical teammates to grow collective National Pharmacy team knowledge and capabilities
  • This position will include job duties that require risk designations for access to Electronic Protected Health Information (PHI) in the course of their job responsibilities
  • Other duties may be assigned

Qualifications:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Required:

  • Bachelor of Science Degree in Pharmacy and/or Doctor of Pharmacy Degree (Pharm.D.) from an accredited U.S. School of Pharmacy
  • Minimum of 3+ years in pharmacy related experience
  • Strong experience in MS Excel with a working knowledge of MS office suite
  • Ability to travel and present to clients and internal teams (travel estimated at 20%)
  • Quick self-motivated learner who can initiate and assist in new projects
  • Above average communication skills (you will be responsible for presenting your work to both internal and external technical and non-technical audiences)
  • Intellectual curiosity — the position requires novel research to keep Brown & Brown’s competitive edge
  • Passion for pharmacy and/or medical data

Preferred:

  • Knowledge, experience and understanding of the PBM/Managed Care Industry
  • Strong analytical and organizational skills
  • Experience with Tableau, including development and adhoc querying
  • Model Development and/or pharmacy data analytics
  • Expertise in SQL, preferably in an Oracle environment
  • Broad understanding of business intelligence, reporting and statistics a plus.
  • Knowledge of PBM benefit design. 
  • Knowledge of product development and release cycles/process is important.

Pay Range

160000 - 168000 Annual

The pay range provided above is made in good faith and based on our lowest and highest annual salary or hourly rate paid for the role and takes into account years of experience required, geography, and/or budget for the role.

Teammate Benefits & Total Well-Being

We go beyond standard benefits, focusing on the total well-being of our teammates, including:

  • Health Benefits: Medical/Rx, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Disability Insurance  
  • Financial Benefits: ESPP; 401k; Student Loan Assistance; Tuition Reimbursement 
  • Mental Health & Wellness: Free Mental Health & Enhanced Advocacy Services
  • Beyond Benefits: Paid Time Off, Holidays, Preferred Partner Discounts and more.

The Power To Be Yourself  

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive environment comprised of people from all backgrounds, with a variety of experiences and perspectives, guided by our Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging (DIB) motto, “The Power to Be Yourself”.

  • Accountable to perform Literature Review as per the applicable organization’s SOP and WI

  • Accountable for recognizing, processing, and reporting Product Quality Complaints (PQC) information as per applicable SOP and WI Accountable for managing Mailboxes including filling emails in appropriate folders

  • Accountable to review and file incoming Faxes in the appropriate folder

  • Accountable to act as a contact point for the client Work directly with internal and external stakeholders to request additional information or clarification as necessary;

  • Assist in audit preparation

  • Other tasks assigned by the Manager, as needed.
